---
title: "Install"
description: "Install Storywell, set up StoryGraph write-back, and register your first source."
---

Storywell is a Python CLI (3.11–3.12). It isn't on PyPI yet, so install it from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/drmowinckels/storywell.git
cd storywell
python -m pip install -e ".[storygraph]"
```

The `[storygraph]` extra pulls in [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/python/) — Storywell writes
to StoryGraph through a real browser session because StoryGraph has no import API. Install the
browser binary once:

```sh
playwright install chromium
```

::: {.callout-note}
Not yet on PyPI. Once released, `pipx install storywell` will be the one-line install.
:::

## Log in to StoryGraph

Log in a single time — Storywell saves the session and reuses it for every later sync:

```sh
storywell storygraph-login          # opens a browser; log in, then return to the terminal
storywell storygraph-status         # check the saved session is still valid
```

## Register a source

Every sync reads from a `--source` (default: `audible`). List what's available:

```sh
storywell sources
```

### Audible

The Audible source uses [`audible-cli`](https://github.com/mkb79/audible-cli) to register your
account once:

```sh
pipx install audible-cli
audible quickstart
```

Storywell reads `~/.audible/config.toml` to find the active profile's auth file. If you use a
non-default profile, pass `--profile <name>`; to bypass discovery entirely, pass
`--auth-file /path/to/profile.json`.

### File & API sources

Goodreads, Kobo, and LibraryThing read a file you already have; Hardcover reads an API. None
need a separate install — you point Storywell at the export or token at run time. See
[Sources](sources.qmd) for where each input comes from.
